newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Safe-haven dollar gains on Bonn-Buba tension.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Safe-haven dollar gains on Bonn-Buba tension.

text.p: The dollar held most of its gains in late European trade on Thursday, buoyed by a row between Bonn and its central bank that has frightened investors into safe-haven currencies.

In equities, Paris stocks closed slightly down after a strong morning rally seemed to have halted this week's big losses. The recent downturn was sparked by fears that the left may be well placed for Sunday's runoff parliamentary elections.

Much of the day's excitement was in currency markets where the mark ended at about 1.70 to the dollar, boosted by its reputation as a shelter in uncertain times after Germany's central bank denounced government plans to revalue its gold reserves.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel earlier reaffirmed the government's intention to pursue the scheme, saying such a revaluation was necessary despite the Bundesbank's objections.
"It's still an uncertain position," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy. "Waigel has reasserted his position and he is unwilling to give ground to the Bundesbank."
Dealers said the revaluation row, seen as a bid by the German government to bolster its finances to help it meet monetary union criteria, had confused markets.

Dollar climbed nearly two pfennigs in eary trade following the German central bank's strong objections on Wednesday to the government's plans, arguing the scheme would only have short-term benefit and would undermine the credibility of EMU.
The U.S. currency eased slightly on Waigel's defence of the plan but was still at 1.7002 marks in late Europe. It earlier hit a session high of 1.7067 after late Wednesday's 1.6905 marks.

Analysts said if the German government succeeds in pushing through its revaluation plans, it raises the prospect of a broad-based EMU with a potentially diluted euro which would be seen as good for the dollar but bad for the mark.
On the other hand, the Bundesbank could make life difficult for the government by being unhelpful over Germany's EMU preparations and raise the risk of a delay to the project.
"Both scenarios are equally likely to happen, the implication is one of volatility," said CIBC's Coleman.
Against the yen, the dollar got a boost from an unexpected fall in Japan's April industrial production, which dampened expectations of higher Japanese rates.

In equity markets, Paris soared by more than one percent at one point after closing down 3.63 percent on Wednesday -- the second big drop of the week prompted by the enhanced prospects for the left in elections on Sunday.
But the market lost early gains and slipped into the minus column at the close, buffeted by rumours of conflicting private opinion polls about Sunday's election runoff. Volume was heavy.
Market talk of a private poll putting the Socialists ahead of the conservative parties eroded the early gains, which had been based on a rumour of an opinion poll putting right-wing parties ahead.
"I don't bother to understand any more. There are no real targets up or down, there are only reactions to rumours," said a trader.

In London, stocks ended with small losses as concerns about the fate of EMU and worries about the outcome of the French elections were balanced by a late advance in the U.S. bond market, dealers and analysts said.

"The problems in Germany and concerns about the French election are all reasons for the market to go lower," said one senior dealer. "But we've seen some selective buying, albeit on tiny volume. The market's performance has been quite encouraging."
A directionless start of Wall Street provided little impetus for UK shares. The Dow opened steady and was down about 25 points when London markets closed.

In Frankfurt, floor trade was closed because of a public holiday. Dealings on the electronic IBIS index closed showing a modest profit, encouraged by the stronger dollar and shrugging off the Bonn-Buba clash.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted at 1.7002 marks and 116.17 yen compared with 1.6902 marks and 115.86 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index finished down 5.2 points at 4,672.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 ended down 3.93 points at 2,579.24.
FRANKFURT - The German bourse was closed for floor trade. In screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index closed up 8.78 points at 3635.38.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was finished at $344.05 an ounce, compared with Wednesday's close of $345.05 in London. Silver was three cents stronger at $4.75 in late trade.
